summary: Christopher Kelley is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD at Columbia University. He taught at Columbia University, The New School, and Brooklyn College, and founded the Columbia Society for Comparative Philosophy.

Christopher Key Chapple works in Indology and religious studies. He served as a professor at the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions (attested 1982) and held the Doshi Professorship of Indic and Comparative Theology at Loyola Marymount University (attested 2001–2017).
Christopher L. Diamond is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied under Heidi R. M. Pauwels from circa 2012 to 2018. He held a post at the Australian National University around 2018.

Christopher Minkowski is an Indologist who studied at Harvard, Delhi, and under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served as a professor at Cornell University (1989–2006) and as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Oxford and Balliol College (2005–2023).

Christopher Pinney is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He has held academic posts at the Australian National University, University College London as professor of anthropology and visual culture, University of Chicago, Northwestern University, University of Cape Town, and Jawaharlal Nehru University.

Christopher S. George is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Columbia University under Royal W. Weiler, Geshe Wangyal, and Pema Gyaltsen, founded the American Institute of Buddhist Studies, and was a professor at IASWR (attested 1982).

Christopher S. Queen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. At Harvard University, he served as Dean of Students for Continuing Education and lecturer on the Study of Religion (circa 1989) and lecturer on Buddhism and World Religions (attested 2013).

Christopher Wallis is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Rochester, Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, and UC Berkeley under Robert P. Goldman and Alexander von Rospatt. He was a guest lecturer at Naropa University (attested 2020).

Chu-tsing Li was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology who studied at the University of Nanking and the University of Iowa. He taught English at Nanking (1943–1947), art history at Iowa (circa 1956–1966), and served on the University of Kansas faculty (1966).
Chuichi Kimura is a Buddhist studies scholar who has held academic posts at Minobusan University, serving as an associate professor (attested 2015) and former professor (attested 2026).

Chun-i Tang was a philosopher and sinologist who studied at Peking University and National Central University. He co-founded New Asia College, taught at National Central University (1944–1949), and was the first Chair Professor at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (1963–1974).
Chun-min Yen is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Arizona under Robert M. Gimello and studied under Todd Brown, Chanyun, and Sheng Yen.
Chung-pui Tai is a scholar of linguistics, sinology, and Tibetology who studied at the Graduate School of Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and held a post at the University of Hong Kong.

Chögyam Trungpa was a Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology figure who studied at Oxford and under teachers including Khenpo Gangshar. He served as spiritual advisor at Young Lamas Home School and founded Samye Ling, Naropa University, and Shambhala International.

Chökyi Gyatso was a scholar who studied under Khakyab Dorje, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.
Chökyi Nyima was a scholar who studied under Dudjom Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Chökyi Nyima Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology scholar who studied at Rumtek Monastery and under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche. He became abbot of Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling in 1976 and founded Rangjung Yeshe Institute in 1981.
Chökyi Nyinche was a scholar who studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Shechen Gyaltsab, and taught Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.
Chönyi Drolma is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Thinley Norbu Rinpoche, Lama Tharchin Rinpoche, and Ngawang Zangpo (all attested 2011).
Chüan-ying Yen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and sinology. She completed her PhD at Harvard University, studying under Chu-tsing Li, John Hay, and John M. Rosenfield.
